neighbours.label: The second member of a parallel contrast, where a new word stands in for its earlier counterpart (entered ... enrolled, screen ... display, the X patch ... the Y memorial)
fire: Thirty runners started the short race, and ninety competed in the long event.
The cheap laptop has a dim panel, far duller than the bright monitor on the desk.
The Harris banner comes down in May, but the Clarke statue is there for good.
In the first group people tasted bread. For the cheese condition, people tasted cheddar.
The frame is not wooden, but could be built from light steel tubing.
Twelve members joined the choir, and twenty signed up for the band class.
The old car had a small boot, much smaller than the wide trunk on the new model.
The summer fee is paid once, but the winter charge is collected every month.
quiet: Ninety runners competed in the long event on Sunday morning.
The bright monitor on the desk was bought for the new designer.
The Clarke statue has stood in the square since the war.
For the cheese tasting, people tried cheddar and drank cider.
The frame could be built from light steel tubing in a week.
Twenty children signed up for the band class this term.
The wide trunk on the new model holds three suitcases easily.
The winter charge is collected every month by the council.

notes: Card peaks have no shared token, but each top example is the matching slot of a second, contrasted clause. Probes of that structure fired 0.37-0.86; the same words in a single clause without the earlier counterpart scored 0.03 ('Sixty students enrolled in the arts course', 'a six-inch display'). Looser parallels with unrelated verbs fired less (0.11, 0.23). The - pole is the other side: a pro-form that repeats the earlier predicate instead of varying it (does so, it is, they can).
